html:
SMTO-JOB-0001 — SMTO can't tell whether a background job ran

GUID: 32dfdb83-c0cd-44a5-ba70-420507e9554c
Slug: job-launch-outcome-unknown
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • A background job SMTO started on a computer may have started or even finished, but SMTO never got confirmation. Starting it again could do the same work twice.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, open Inspect execution for this step and look at its status and latest output. It shows the last thing SMTO recorded about the job, including any output it produced.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to check the status of the earlier job, not to start a new one. SMTO can ask the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) what happened to that same job without running it again.
  3. Check the computer the job ran on for its results, such as files it should have made or a service it should have changed. What actually changed on that computer is the surest sign of whether the work happened.
  4. Only if you confirm the work did not happen, ask SMTO to run the job again. This keeps the same work from being done twice.

What success looks like

  • You know whether the job's work happened, and a new run starts only if it didn't.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't start the same job again while its outcome is still unknown.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway job's launch or execution outcome is unknown: launch may have crossed dispatch without a confirmed acknowledgement, or the worker could not record trustworthy completion.

What this means

  • Job launch may have crossed dispatch without a confirmed acknowledgement, or the worker could not record trustworthy execution completion and marks its state unknown. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • Job launch may have crossed dispatch without a confirmed acknowledgement, or the worker could not record trustworthy execution completion and marks its state unknown.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original Gateway job identity, dispatch fence, supervisor/process state and retained completion evidence.

How to fix it

  • The job is in state unknown/outcome_unknown (job_contract.uncertain from GatewayJobs.start or the worker). Run manage_job inspect, reconcile or logs on the original job_id and check the target host before any new launch; missing output or a failed control does not prove the process stopped.
  • Inspect and reconcile the original job's authoritative state before requesting any additional launch.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original job outcome is reconciled through supported observation before any new launch.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
  • SMTO-GWT-0026 — Gateway job control unavailable
  • SMTO-JOB-0016 — The Gateway couldn't start this background job
